Lam Wing-kee was one of five booksellers who disappeared in 2015. His subsequent revelations about his detention by Chinese authorities made him a prominent voice for freedom of speech in Hong Kong and later in Taiwan.

The Poison:
The loss of such a voice is a stark reminder of the narrowing space for dissent and the personal costs borne by those who challenge authoritarian narratives.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:

Lam's life was a rejection of the 'selfish loop' of authoritarian power. By choosing transparency about his detention, he empowered others to recognize the fragility of their own freedoms.

The Unavoidable Truth: Freedom of speech is often defended by the most ordinary people.

The Unavoidable Lie: That political repression is a thing of the past.
